drivingQuestion: Whose view is followed — the first tanna, who requires dismounting when someone can hold the donkey, or Rabbi, who does not?
outcomeNote: The halakha is fixed like Rabbi; only the attribution of the ruling is left with two versions.

segments.he: אָמַר רָבָא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי.
segments.en: «Rava, and some say Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, said:» The «halakha» here «is in accordance with» the opinion of «Rabbi» Yehuda HaNasi.

moves.cueHe: אמר רבא, ואיתימא רבי יהושע בן לוי: הלכה כרבי
moves.summary: decides the baraita's dispute of the previous unit in favour of Rabbi
moves.about: whether the halakha for one riding a donkey when the time for prayer arrives follows Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi, who says he prays where he sits

edges.about: whether the halakha for one riding a donkey when the time for prayer arrives follows Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi, who says he prays where he sits
an alternative attribution of the ruling that the halakha follows Rabbi
edges.proposedPredicate: transmit.attributes_alternatively_to — «ואיתימא» — reassigns a tradition already reported in one Sage's name to a different Sage as a competing version
